articles.title: Binance Wins In-Principle Approval for Asia Hub in Bhutan's Gelephu
articles.excerpt: It isn't a full licence yet: Binance must meet Gelephu Central Bank's conditions first. The exchange holds licences in 15 markets, Reuters reported.
articles.body_md:
Binance has cleared the first regulatory step toward an Asia hub in Bhutan. Gelephu Central Bank granted the exchange in-principle approval to run regulated digital-asset operations in Gelephu Mindfulness City, Binance said in a [statement dated Nov. 28](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/binance-secures-in-principle-approval-in-gelephu-mindfulness-city-plans-asia-hub-in-bhutan-302952037.html).

It isn't a licence to trade yet. Binance "must satisfy the conditions specified by GCB and complete the remaining regulatory requirements before the relevant regulated activities may commence," the statement said. [Reuters](https://www.straitstimes.com/business/binance-gets-preliminary-approval-to-establish-asia-hub-in-bhutan) carried the same caveat.

**How Gelephu's two-step licence works**

Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC) is a special administrative region in southern Bhutan with its own financial rulebook. Under the Gelephu Financial Services Act 2025, crypto businesses sit under the same rules as banks and brokers, and running an order-book exchange (a venue that matches buyers and sellers) needs a Financial Services Licence, the [GMC licensing FAQ](https://gmc.bt/GFSO/faqs) says.

An in-principle approval is the halfway mark. The FAQ says it doesn't allow any regulated activity until conditions are met, such as setting up a local company and opening a bank account inside the zone. Neither Binance nor GMC said which conditions apply in this case or when a full licence might follow.

**Hiring and training in Bhutan**

Binance and GMC also signed a cooperation agreement at Binance Blockchain Week 2026. The exchange said it plans a "substantive operational presence" in Bhutan, with local hiring and training in compliance and operations. It gave no headcount or investment figure.

Bhutan isn't new ground for the company. Binance launched a crypto payment system for tourists there in 2025, the statement said.

**An expansion push after the October hack**

Binance holds operating licences in 15 markets and is in talks with "at least five or six markets," Asia-Pacific head SB Seker told [Reuters](https://www.straitstimes.com/business/binance-gets-preliminary-approval-to-establish-asia-hub-in-bhutan). The approval comes a month after hackers took an estimated $6.3 billion from the exchange on Oct. 29. Black Mint [reported Nov. 26](https://blackmint.markets/news/binance-withdrawals-resume-hack/) that Binance had finished restoring withdrawals.

*In our opinion: an in-principle approval opens the door only partway. GMC's own FAQ puts the usual wait for this stage at six to eight months after an application, and the full licence still sits on the other side of conditions nobody has published. The document worth waiting for is that Financial Services Licence, because until it lands, no Binance customer can trade a thing through Gelephu.*

articles.title: WLFI Falls 53% After World Liberty Wallet Sells $20 Million in Ether
articles.excerpt: World Liberty's token hit a record low near $0.0167 after a project wallet sold ether and repaid part of a Dolomite loan. Justin Sun called for delistings.
articles.body_md:
World Liberty Financial's WLFI token fell 53.4% in 24 hours to about $0.0191 at 5:53 a.m. ET Saturday, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/world-liberty-financial), after touching a record low of $0.0167 shortly before 1 a.m. ET. That leaves it about 94% below its September 2025 high of $0.331.

The drop followed an ether sale by a project treasury wallet. [OnchainBeat](https://onchainbeat.com/news/2026/11/world-liberty-sells-10-600-eth-pays-down-dolomite-loans/), which checked the transactions on Etherscan, said the wallet sold 10,600 ETH and 1,378 mETH, a staked-ether token, for about $20.1 million in USDC and USD1 on Friday evening, UTC. It said about $16.59 million in USDC then went to the lending protocol Dolomite to pay down a loan, a transfer [Bitcoin.com News](https://news.bitcoin.com/crypto-news/world-liberty-financial-sells-12121-eth-19-million-loss/) also reported. On-chain analyst EmberCN estimated the ether was bought last year near $3,244 a coin, implying a loss of about $19.26 million. [Mempool Brief](https://mempoolbrief.com/articles/world-liberty-financial-wallet-sells-20-million-in-ethereum-for-stablecoins) said that figure is an on-chain estimate, not an audited result.

**How a token loan works**

On Dolomite, a borrower posts tokens as collateral and borrows stablecoins against them. If that collateral loses too much value, the position can be sold off automatically; repaying part of the loan lowers that risk. In April, World Liberty pledged about 5 billion WLFI to borrow $75 million, [crypto.news](https://crypto.news/justin-sun-wlfi-usd1-delisting/) and [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/28/trump-linked-crypto-token-wlfi-plunges-over-50) reported.

USD1, the project's dollar stablecoin, dipped to about $0.94 early Saturday, both outlets reported, and was back at $0.998 at 5:53 a.m. ET on CoinGecko.

**Sun's allegations and the other side**

Tron founder Justin Sun, an early investor who [sued World Liberty in April](https://crypto.news/justin-sun-wlfi-usd1-delisting/) over frozen tokens, alleged in an X post that insiders had sold tokens improperly and defrauded investors, and urged exchanges to delist WLFI and USD1. His post gave no wallet addresses or transaction details, crypto.news said. World Liberty, which is backed by the Trump family, gave a different account in a May lawsuit against Sun, saying its token restrictions were allowed under its sale terms and accusing him of a campaign to push the price down. The company had not commented on Saturday's sale, according to CoinDesk and Bitcoin.com News.

*In our opinion: The company has not explained the sale, so the on-chain record is the only account readers have. The pressure point is the collateral: the April loan was backed by about 5 billion WLFI, and that token lost half its value overnight. Watch for a World Liberty statement, any exchange response to Sun's call, and whether USD1 keeps trading at $1.*

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Shed Record $5.78 Billion in November; BTC Under $60K
articles.excerpt: Friday's $389 million exit made eight straight days of outflows and pushed November past June's $4.51 billion record. Bitcoin traded near $59,150.
articles.body_md:
U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds have lost a net $5.78 billion in November, the most for any month since they launched in January 2024, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/bitcoin-etf-flow-all-data/) data through Friday show. The prior record was $4.51 billion, in June 2026.

Friday added $389.0 million of outflows, the eighth straight trading day of net withdrawals. BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $327.2 million of that, Farside data show. [The Crypto Times](https://www.cryptotimes.io/2026/11/28/bitcoin-price-slips-below-60k-as-411m-crypto-liquidations-hit-long-traders/), citing SoSoValue and Farside, reported the same Friday total and monthly record.

Bitcoin traded at $59,150 at 5:55 a.m. ET Saturday, down 4.0% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). It ranged from $58,910 to $61,752 in that window. On Friday it gave up its Thanksgiving gains, falling from above $62,000 to below $59,000, [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/cryptocurrency-news/bitcoin-price-today-falls-below-60k-as-whales-buy-dip-etf-outflows-mount-5054180) reported. The coin is up 2.1% over seven days but down 26.2% over 30 days, CoinGecko data show.

**How fund outflows work**

A spot bitcoin ETF holds actual bitcoin for its shareholders. A net outflow means more shares were redeemed than created that day, so the funds shrink and the bitcoin behind those shares leaves them. Farside tallies those daily changes fund by fund.

Borrowed bets felt the drop too. More than $400 million of leveraged crypto positions were forcibly closed over 24 hours, most of them bets on higher prices, according to CoinGlass figures cited by The Crypto Times ($411.69 million as of 4:19 a.m. ET) and [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/crypto-liquidations-407-million-coinglass/) ($407 million). A liquidation happens when an exchange closes a trader's position because the posted collateral no longer covers the loss.

The Crypto Fear & Greed Index stood at 10, its "Extreme Fear" band, on Saturday, according to [Alternative.me](https://alternative.me/crypto/fear-and-greed-index/). The Federal Reserve's next rate meeting is Dec. 8-9, per its [calendar](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm).

*In our opinion: The number that matters is $5.78 billion, about $1.3 billion more than the old monthly record, with one trading day of November still to go. Bitcoin is still up for the week, but the funds have not shared in that bounce. Monday's Farside print and the Dec. 8-9 Fed meeting are the next two dates worth circling. The exits are well marked; the entrance could use a sign.*

articles.title: November Jobs Report Due Friday as Fed Enters Pre-Meeting Quiet Period
articles.excerpt: The jobs report lands at 8:30 a.m. ET Dec. 4, with ISM surveys and JOLTS earlier in the week. Fed officials entered their blackout before the Dec. 8-9 meeting.
articles.body_md:
The November jobs report is due at 8:30 a.m. ET Friday, Dec. 4, closing a week of U.S. data that starts with Federal Reserve officials in their pre-meeting quiet period, according to the [Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/12_sched_list.htm) and [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm) calendars. The Fed's last rate meeting of 2026 is Dec. 8-9.

**The calendar, Nov. 28 to Dec. 4 (all times ET)**

- **Saturday, Nov. 28, 12:00 a.m.:** The Fed's blackout period began. Under its [communications policy](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/files/FOMC_ExtCommunicationParticipants.pdf), it starts the second Saturday before a meeting and ends at 11:59 p.m. the day after, here Dec. 10.
- **Monday, Nov. 30:** Last trading day of November for U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs, which had net outflows of $5.78 billion for the month through Nov. 27, per [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/bitcoin-etf-flow-all-data/).
- **Tuesday, Dec. 1, 10:00 a.m.:** ISM Manufacturing PMI for November, per the [Institute for Supply Management](https://www.ismworld.org/supply-management-news-and-reports/reports/rob-report-calendar/), and the BLS job openings report (JOLTS) for October. Eurostat's flash euro area inflation estimate for November is also scheduled that day, per its [October release](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-euro-indicators/w/2-18112026-ap).
- **Thursday, Dec. 3, 10:00 a.m.:** ISM Services PMI.
- **Friday, Dec. 4, 8:30 a.m.:** BLS Employment Situation for November.

**What these reports measure**

A PMI, or purchasing managers' index, is ISM's monthly survey of purchasing executives at U.S. companies, one for factories and one for service businesses. JOLTS, short for Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, counts open jobs, hires and departures. The Employment Situation report gives the month's payroll job change and the unemployment rate.

During the blackout, Fed policymakers hold off on public comments about monetary policy, under the same policy, so the week's economic news comes from these releases. The Dec. 8-9 meeting includes new economic projections, the Fed calendar shows, and November consumer prices follow on Dec. 10, per BLS.

Bitcoin stood at $59,150 at 5:55 a.m. ET Saturday, down 4.0% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: With Fed officials silent, Friday's payroll number is the headline the market gets before Dec. 9. The other date on our list is Monday, when Farside posts the last November tally for the ETF record. No forecast here, only the calendar.*

articles.title: ECB's Vujčić Sees Market Bets on December Rate Hike Proving Accurate
articles.excerpt: The ECB vice president told Kurier that market bets on a December increase will probably prove accurate. The deposit rate is 2.50% and October inflation was 4.0%.
articles.body_md:
European Central Bank Vice President Boris Vujčić said investors expecting a rate increase at the bank's Dec. 16-17 meeting would probably be proved right, in a joint interview with Austria's Kurier that the ECB posted on Saturday. The ECB's deposit rate is 2.50%, after increases in June and September, [ECB data](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/key_ecb_interest_rates/html/index.en.html) show.

Asked whether a hike could be assumed given high inflation, Vujčić said "market expectations are likely to prove accurate," provided nothing unexpected happens before the meeting, according to the [ECB's English transcript](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/inter/date/2026/html/ecb.in261128~10e11f78f1.en.html) of the interview, which also included Austrian central bank Governor Martin Kocher. [Econostream](https://www.econostream-media.com/news/2026-11-28/ecb%E2%80%99s_vuj%C4%8Di%C4%87_expects_markets_to_be_right_about_december_rate_hike.html) and [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/ecb-officials-signal-further-rate-hikes-as-inflation-remains-elevated-5054086) reported the remarks as pointing to a December increase, which both said markets expect.

Kocher said that the longer higher energy prices last, the greater the chance of "second-round effects," and that the ECB "can't allow our interest rate decisions to be overtaken by events." Euro area inflation was 4.0% in October, up from 3.8% in September, with energy prices up 21.0%, according to [Eurostat](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-euro-indicators/w/2-18112026-ap). The ECB targets 2% over the medium term.

**What the deposit rate does**

The deposit rate is what banks earn on money parked overnight at the ECB. Raising it pushes up borrowing and savings rates across the euro area, which the ECB uses to slow spending and bring inflation back toward target. A "second-round effect" is when an energy price jump feeds into wages and other prices, keeping inflation high after the original shock.

Vujčić also said euro area growth had come in stronger than forecasters expected and was running near its potential rate. The ECB's [meeting calendar](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/calendars/mgcgc/html/index.en.html) lists the Governing Council's monetary policy meeting for Dec. 16-17 in Frankfurt.

Bitcoin was priced at $59,150 at 5:55 a.m. ET Saturday, down 4.0% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: When the ECB's No. 2 says the market has it right three weeks out, he is showing which way he leans, with a caveat for surprises. A quarter-point move, the size of the June and September increases, would take the deposit rate to 2.75%. The next checkpoint is Eurostat's November flash inflation estimate, scheduled for Dec. 1, and then the decision itself on Dec. 17.*

articles.title: Anza Urges Solana Validators to Install Agave v4.4.2 Right Away
articles.excerpt: The patch updates the QUIC networking code validators use to talk to each other. Anza said Solana's clusters were running normally.
articles.body_md:
Anza, the company that develops Solana's Agave validator software, told mainnet node operators on Friday, Nov. 27, to install Agave v4.4.2 immediately. "Don't wait, upgrade now," Anza [posted on X](https://x.com/anza_xyz/status/2126458885674533324) at 6:31 p.m. ET, adding that "clusters are safe and running normally."

The alert covers every Agave-based node, staked or unstaked. Operators on Solana's testnet and devnet were told to move to v4.5.0-rc.1, a release candidate [published on GitHub](https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/releases/tag/v4.5.0-rc.1) the same day.

**What the patch changes**

Validators are the computers that check transactions and produce blocks on Solana. They take in transactions over QUIC, an internet transport protocol, according to [Anza's documentation](https://docs.anza.xyz/validator/tpu). Agave ships its own copy of quinn, an open-source Rust library that implements QUIC.

The [v4.4.2 release notes](https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/releases/tag/v4.4.2), posted at 2:04 p.m. ET, list a bump of those "anza-quinn" crates as the main change. The [pull request](https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/pull/17131) says the crates "need a fix backported from upstream quinn." That upstream fix, [quinn pull request 3030](https://github.com/quinn-rs/quinn/pull/3030), is titled "handle large number of unacked packets." Unacked packets are pieces of data a computer has sent but the other side has not yet confirmed receiving.

Anza's [backport](https://github.com/anza-xyz/quinn/pull/21), merged at 11:31 a.m. ET, says the upstream pull request was still open. Anza said nothing else changes in v4.4.2 "beyond small backports," in a [follow-up post](https://x.com/anza_xyz/status/2126458886748246516). It did not publicly describe what could happen to a node that skips the update.

**Other clients follow**

Jito-Solana and Harmonic, two validator clients built on Agave code, released their own v4.4.2-based versions, Anza said. [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/anza-urges-immediate-agave-upgrade-on-solana-mainnet) also reported both releases. Solana co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko shared the alert on X with the words "[Upgrade pls!!!](https://x.com/toly/status/2126463636046741900)"

*In our opinion: The bigger story is the speed. Anza's backport and the mainnet release landed about two and a half hours apart on the Friday after Thanksgiving, for a fix that was still under review in the upstream library. Operators are patching on the strength of the warning alone, because Anza has not said what an unpatched node risks. The next thing to watch is whether Anza publishes a fuller explanation once the upgrade has spread across the network.*

articles.title: SafePal Adds 37,542 Older Order Records to August Data Breach
articles.excerpt: The wallet maker says it deleted the records needed to email this group, so buyers from Sept. 2022 to March 2025 should treat their details as exposed.
articles.body_md:
Crypto wallet maker SafePal said in an update dated Nov. 28 that a data breach it first disclosed in August reached further back than it reported, adding 37,542 order-related records from purchases made between Sept. 6, 2022, and March 1, 2025.

The update, posted to SafePal's [security page](https://www.safepal.com/en/blog/security-update), says the company began looking again after reports on Nov. 25 of phishing emails sent to customers whose orders fell outside the original window. The figure counts records, including refunds and failed orders, and is "not 37,542 unique customers," SafePal said.

**What was exposed**

For the newly found group, SafePal said the data was limited to names, email addresses, countries, order IDs, products bought and payment IDs. It said shipping addresses, phone numbers, card or bank details, wallet payment addresses, recovery phrases and private keys were not part of it. [TechFlow](https://www.techflowpost.com/en-US/newsletter/147312/safepal-data-breach-expands-37542-order-records) and [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/safepal-extends-august-breach-disclosure-to-older-orders) also reported the update.

SafePal said this is an expansion of the same incident, not a new breach. It said the original authorization flaw, a gap in who could view order data, was fixed in August, and that security firm Cure53 found no remaining vulnerabilities in an audit completed Oct. 30. The earlier disclosed window, orders from March 2, 2025, to April 11, 2026, is unchanged.

**Why buyers will not get an email**

A recovery phrase is the list of words that can restore a wallet and move its funds on any device. Order data cannot open a wallet, but it can make a fake message look real. SafePal said it deleted the customer records needed to contact this group under its data policy, so it cannot notify them one by one. It asked buyers from that period to "consider their information potentially affected." On Nov. 12, the company warned of physical letters with QR codes leading to phishing sites.

SafePal said it will never ask for a recovery phrase or private keys, and urged users to ignore unofficial firmware-update instructions.

*In our opinion: What raises the risk for buyers is the combination of real order details and no direct warning. Anyone who bought from SafePal between September 2022 and March 2025 has to find this notice on their own. The practical step is the one the company lists: never type a recovery phrase into any site, email or QR-code page, whatever order number it quotes.*

articles.title: Nvidia Ends Up 0.8% After Intraday Dip, Bloomberg China Chip Report
articles.excerpt: Bloomberg's report on Blackwell hardware at a Shanghai site tied to Alice Huang came before the open, yet Nvidia closed higher. What the filings show.
articles.body_md:
Nvidia stock fell as much as 2.6% on Friday, then recovered to close up 0.8% at $150.49, on a day Bloomberg reported that Blackwell-based hardware appears in Chinese loan filings for a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA/history/) and [Nvidia's investor page](https://investor.nvidia.com/stock-info/stock-quote-and-chart/) both show a low of $145.39 against Wednesday's $149.30 close. U.S. markets were closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, and trading ended at 1 p.m. ET Friday.

The chart below is Black Mint's, built from those two sources. It adds Friday's story to our [midweek note](https://blackmint.markets/news/where-the-money-went-midweek-nov-23) on Nvidia's Monday rally.

**What Bloomberg's filings show**

[Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-27/nvidia-blackwell-chips-turn-up-at-china-site-tied-to-alice-huang) published its report at 6:45 a.m. ET. It says two Chinese companies listed Blackwell hardware at the Yangtze River Delta Project in Shanghai, in documents filed with Chinese regulators and lenders.

- Shanghai Shuoyao offered a GB300 NVL72 rack, which holds 72 Blackwell Ultra chips, as collateral for a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank. The rack's serial number appears in November filings.
- Shanghai Kezhan described a GB200 server at the site when it took a 90 million yuan loan in late 2025 from a leasing firm owned by a Shanghai government agency.

Bloomberg typed the serial number into a public warranty database, which traced it to Taiwan's Gigabyte Technology. Gigabyte declined to say who bought the rack first and said it follows applicable laws. [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2329748/restricted-nvidia-chips-were-installed-at-a-chinese-data-center-linked-to-alice-huang/) and [Anadolu](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/science-technology/nvidia-blackwell-chips-found-at-china-data-center-linked-to-alice-huang-report/4140762) carried the same details. Blackwell chips need a U.S. license to ship to China, and President Donald Trump has said he does not want them sent there for now, Bloomberg reported.

**What the report leaves open**

Nobody has shown how or when the rack reached China. Bloomberg said the gear often passes through several hands before it is installed, and that Nvidia did not answer its questions. Bloomberg also said it found no evidence that Megaspeed, the Singapore cloud company Alice Huang once ran, sent the hardware to the site. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing, and Shuoyao called its tie to Megaspeed "ordinary commercial cooperation."

The filings are Chinese loan records that Bloomberg reviewed, and they are not public. Black Mint could not see them, so every fact above about their contents is Bloomberg's account.

**Who Alice Huang is, and what is alleged**

Alice Huang is the former Megaspeed chief executive whose affair with Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang led to his resignation, [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/us-to-blacklist-alibaba-subsidiary-and-megaspeed-linked-to-nvidia-scandal-5046337) reported. The resignation came Nov. 12, [Quartz](https://qz.com/nvidia-blackwell-chips-shanghai-data-center-alice-huang-112726) said, and the two Huangs are not related. U.S. authorities suspect she acted for Chinese intelligence, and China calls that groundless. Singapore said it investigated her over possible false declarations in server purchases, not espionage. Megaspeed says she left in August 2025. Reuters could not reach her for comment.

Among other ties, Bloomberg points to Kang Wei, the facility's president. [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/exclusivealice-huanglinked-firms-listed-270-million-in-ai-servers-in-china-records-show-5049792) identifies him as her husband. In a separate Nov. 25 report, Reuters found central-bank credit records listing up to 764 AI servers and modules worth $270 million at firms tied to her family and associates, much of it at a Shanghai site called the Yangtze River Delta AI supercomputing centre. Those records do not show whether the servers held chips barred from export.

**The week around the report**

Nvidia closed at $125.53 on Nov. 20 and $165.05 on Nov. 23, the day its board reinstated Jensen Huang. It is down 26.5% from its Oct. 30 close of $204.64, Yahoo Finance data show.

- Nov. 23: the Commerce Department added seven entities to its Entity List, including Megaspeed units and Alibaba's Singapore subsidiary Apex, citing a significant risk of chip diversion, the [Federal Register](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/25/2026-23999/additions-to-the-entity-list) says. Alibaba called the Apex listing erroneous, [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/factboxwhat-we-know-about-megaspeed-the-nvidia-customer-blacklisted-by-us-5047829) reported.
- Nov. 25: S&P Global Ratings put Nvidia's AA rating on CreditWatch Negative over governance, [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/sp-global-places-nvidia-rating-on-creditwatch-negative-on-rising-management-and-governance-risks-5051352) and [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-25/s-p-says-it-may-downgrade-nvidia-s-ratings-on-governance-worries) reported.
- Nov. 26: Nvidia told server partners to stop shipping to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, the Financial Times reported, per [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/nvidia-halts-server-shipments-southeast-asia-ft-reports-5052112).

Friday's volume through the 1 p.m. close was 185.8 million shares. No single cause for the dip is confirmed. [Investor's Business Daily](https://www.investors.com/news/technology/nvidia-stock-jensen-huang-testimony/) pointed to the Southeast Asia halt and next week's testimony, along with the Bloomberg story.

**What comes next**

Huang is due for a closed-door interview with three House committees on Dec. 1, and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter on Dec. 2, the [House Select Committee on the CCP](https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/media/press-releases/jensen-huang-and-nvidia-agree-to-appear-before-congress) and [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/17/nvidia-jensen-huang-house-committee.html) said. The Senate Banking Committee has scheduled Huang for a public hearing at 10 a.m. ET on Dec. 3, titled "Protecting America's AI Advantage: Oversight of U.S. Export Controls," the [committee's hearing notice](https://www.banking.senate.gov/hearings/protecting-americas-ai-advantage-oversight-of-us-export-controls) and [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jensen-huang-congress-reinstatement-nvidia/) show.

*In our opinion: Friday's price action says less than the headline did, since the stock gave back its dip within hours. The open question is who first bought that rack from Gigabyte, and neither the filings nor the companies have answered it. We will be following Dec. 1 closely, because the committee chairs said they want answers on how Nvidia's chips reached Chinese users.*

articles.title: Block Reaches $442.5 Million Deal to Settle Shareholder Lawsuit
articles.excerpt: Cash App's parent disclosed the investor deal in an SEC filing Friday. It still needs court approval and sits apart from a pending $764 million DOJ deal.
articles.body_md:
Block, the company behind Cash App and Square, has agreed in principle to pay about $442.5 million to settle a shareholder class action, it said in a Friday filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The deal still needs preliminary and final approval from a federal judge in California. It covers investors who bought Block's Class A stock between Feb. 26, 2020, and Aug. 1, 2024, according to the [Form 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1512673/000119312526480257/d66844d8k.htm).

**The suit is about compliance statements**

The shareholders allege Block made false or misleading statements about its anti-money laundering and compliance programs, the company's [quarterly report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1512673/000162828026069524/xyz-20260930.htm) says. Block asked the court to throw the case out. A judge denied that request on Jan. 6, 2026. The two sides reached the agreement on Nov. 17.

How this works: in a securities class action, a few investors sue for everyone who bought in a set window. An "agreement in principle" means the main terms are set but the final papers aren't signed. The 8-K is silent on liability.

**A second, larger deal is also pending**

The settlement is separate from a Justice Department matter. In October, Block reached an agreement in principle with the DOJ on a deferred prosecution agreement over a charge that it failed to keep an effective anti-money laundering program under the Bank Secrecy Act, the quarterly report says. A deferred prosecution agreement means prosecutors hold off on the charge for a set period, here three years, and drop it if the company meets its terms.

That deal carries a gross figure of about $964 million and a net payment of about $764 million after credit for earlier regulatory settlements. Block had set aside $764 million for it as of Sept. 30. Like the investor deal, it needs a final agreement and court approval. The SEC told Block in March that it had ended its own investigation without recommending action, the filing says.

Why crypto readers care: Cash App lets customers buy and sell bitcoin, and Block holds the keys for coins it keeps for them, per the quarterly report. Neither settlement is tied to bitcoin trading in the filings.

*In our opinion: the number that matters is about $1.2 billion. That's the two proposed deals added together, both still waiting on a judge. The next step to watch is the request for preliminary court approval, where the full settlement terms are filed.*

articles.title: Russia's VTB Opens Crypto Trading to Qualified Investors in App
articles.excerpt: The state-majority bank's clients must pass a new Bank of Russia-approved test and hold coins in VTB's own depository. Moscow Exchange plans crypto trading on Dec. 1.
articles.body_md:
Russian bank VTB opened crypto buying and selling to brokerage clients in its VTB My Investments app on Friday, Nov. 27, a day after the Bank of Russia approved a mandatory knowledge test for crypto buyers.

Access is narrow for now. Clients need qualified investor status, a legal category for people who meet wealth or experience thresholds, and must also pass the new test, [RBC](https://www.rbc.ru/quote/27/11/2026/6b087dd64e4ce3ce0a252ce7) and [Bitcoin Magazine](https://bitcoinmagazine.com/news/russia-vtb-bitcoin-trading-crypto-test) reported, citing the broker. Trades are over the counter, meaning VTB deals with the client directly rather than matching orders on an exchange.

**The bank holds the coins**

VTB handles the purchase and safekeeping itself, on Russian infrastructure. Clients must open a separate account at VTB's digital depository, where the assets sit, on top of a regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6, according to [CRYPT.ru](https://crypt.ru/news/27-11-2026/vtb-zapustil-sdelki-s-kriptovaljutoj-no-dostup-poluchat-ne-vse-klienty/) and Bitcoin Magazine.

Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said the test would appear in the app on launch day and work like the bank's tests for other instruments. He said VTB would start with buying and selling and add services as regulation develops, per RBC.

The test has eight questions, CRYPT.ru and Bitcoin Magazine reported. NAUFOR, the industry's self-regulatory group, has three days after the standard's approval to send brokers the questions and answers.

**U.S. sanctions still apply to VTB**

The U.S. Treasury imposed full blocking sanctions on VTB in February 2022, saying the bank (majority-owned by the Russian government) held nearly 20% of Russia's banking assets, according to its [press release](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy0608). Blocking sanctions freeze a target's U.S. assets and generally bar Americans from dealing with it. VTB's launch serves Russian clients through Russian infrastructure.

Exchange trading comes next. Moscow Exchange plans to open crypto trading on Dec. 1. The first coins listed: bitcoin, ether and Tether's USDT, RBC reported.

*In our opinion: the bigger story is Russia moving crypto trading onto domestic banks and exchanges, with those banks as custodians. For now only qualified investors who pass the test can use the VTB channel. The date to watch is Dec. 1, when Moscow Exchange is set to open crypto trading.*

articles.title: S&P 500 Gains 5.6% in Holiday Week as Bitcoin ETF Outflows Continue
articles.excerpt: Stocks had their best week since April 2025, yet investors pulled $22.7 billion from global stock funds and $1.25 billion from bitcoin ETFs.
articles.body_md:
Stocks had their best week in more than a year, but the measured money mostly moved the other way. The S&P 500 closed Friday's shortened session at 7,297.49, up 5.6% from the Nov. 20 close and its biggest weekly gain since April 2025, [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/wall-st-futures-surge-as-investors-return-from-holiday-5053052) and the [AP](https://apnews.com/article/stock-markets-tariffs-ai-profits-energy-c7ef10c1dbc5fa09668bd4fe0729c613) reported. In the week to Nov. 25, investors pulled a net $22.73 billion from global equity funds, the most in 14 months, LSEG Lipper data show.

This is the weekly follow-up to our [November "Where the Money Went" deep dive](https://blackmint.markets/news/where-the-money-went-november-deep-dive) and the [midweek note](https://blackmint.markets/news/where-the-money-went-midweek-nov-23) on Monday's Nvidia rally. U.S. markets were closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, and stocks closed at 1 p.m. ET Friday. Several flow reports for the final days of the week were not out by publication time, and we say so below where it matters.

**The weekly scoreboard**

Change from the Nov. 20 close to the Nov. 27 close, from Yahoo Finance data, with the index moves also checked against Reuters and [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/26/stock-market-today-live-updates.html). Bitcoin and ether are compared at 4 p.m. ET both Fridays, using Yahoo Finance and [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin):

- Materials fund (XLB): up 7.9%
- Technology fund (XLK): up 7.5%
- Nasdaq Composite: up 6.7%
- S&P 500: up 5.6%
- Dow: up 5.5%
- Ether: up 4.3% (4.1% on CoinGecko)
- Comex gold: up 3.5%
- Bitcoin: up 2.7% (2.5% on CoinGecko)
- Consumer staples fund (XLP): up 2.5%
- U.S. dollar index: up 0.2%
- 7-10 year Treasury fund (IEF): flat
- WTI crude oil: down 1.1%

All 11 Select Sector SPDR funds rose, led by materials, technology and communication services, Yahoo Finance data show. In Morningstar's sector indexes, basic materials and communication services led, up 7.74% and 7.43%.

**How it works: prices and flows are different things**

A price move does not, by itself, send dollars in or out. Every trade has a buyer and a seller, so the cash only changes hands. When prices fall, holders lose value on paper and that value is simply gone; when prices rise, it comes back the same way. Flows are different. They count dollars that actually moved into or out of a fund, a stablecoin or a share sale. This week shows why both matter: prices rose almost everywhere, while several of the flow reports showed money leaving.

**Stocks: the bounce and the exits**

The week opened with Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive, which lifted the stock 31% on Monday and gave the S&P 500 and Nasdaq their best day since April 2025, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/26/stock-market-today-live-updates.html) reported. Tech gave back part of that on Tuesday and Wednesday before rising again Friday. The Nasdaq gained 6.68% for the week and the Dow 5.46%, [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/wall-st-futures-surge-as-investors-return-from-holiday-5053052) reported, matching Yahoo Finance data.

The fund flow reports out so far show investors selling. Global equity funds lost a net $22.73 billion in the week to Nov. 25, the most since September 2025, and U.S. equity funds lost $30.57 billion, the most since Sept. 9, LSEG Lipper data show, per [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/global-equity-funds-log-biggest-weekly-outflow-in-14-months-5053188) and [PiQ Markets](https://piqmarkets.com/story/global-equity-funds-post-22-73b-weekly-outflow-largest-in-14-months). Technology funds lost $7.57 billion. European equity funds took in $7.29 billion. That Lipper week runs Thursday to Wednesday, so it includes the Nov. 19-20 selloff and not Friday's gains.

No U.S. IPOs priced during the holiday week, [Renaissance Capital](https://www.renaissancecapital.com/IPO-Center/News/122891/us-ipo-weekly-recap-anthropic-delivers-volatile-trading-in-the-quiet) reported. Anthropic, which raised $93.5 billion in its IPO the week before, closed below its $83 offer price on Tuesday and Wednesday, then finished Friday at $91.88, Yahoo Finance data show.

**Bonds and the dollar**

Treasuries ended the week slightly lower in price. The 10-year yield rose to 4.94% from 4.92%, and the 2-year yield rose to 4.69% from 4.63%, [Treasury Department](https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value_month=202611) data show. [TreasuryBonds.com](https://treasurybonds.com/news/2026-11-27-bond-market-wrap-up-treasuries-slide-on-friday-ending-the-holiday-week-with-losses/) put the 10-year at 4.93% and said the 2-year rose the most. When yields rise, bond prices fall.

Bond fund buyers still showed up. Government bond funds took in a net $7.14 billion in the week to Nov. 25, while global bond funds as a group lost $3.51 billion, LSEG Lipper data show, per [Reuters](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/global-equity-funds-log-biggest-weekly-outflow-14-months).

The dollar index rose 0.4% Friday to 104.05, up 0.2% for the week, TreasuryBonds.com reported, in line with Yahoo Finance's 104.01 late Friday. It touched a 22-month high of 104.53 earlier in the week, [Reuters](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/dollar-set-flat-week-haven-bids-counter-yields) reported. Fed funds futures priced about a 99% chance of a December rate hike on Friday, [Reuters](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/risk-sensitive-currencies-rise-tech-rebound-dollar-set-weekly-gain) reported.

**Gold and oil**

Comex December gold settled at $3,639.60, up 3.53% for the week, its biggest weekly gain since the week ended Nov. 6, [Dow Jones Market Data](https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202611274508/comex-gold-ends-the-week-353-higher-at-363960-data-talk) show. The December contract had settled at its 2026 low of $3,512.30 on Nov. 20, the Dow Jones data show. Investors still pulled $2.14 billion from gold and precious metals funds in the week to Nov. 25, the most since March, LSEG Lipper data show.

U.S. crude settled at $83.08 a barrel on Friday, down about 1% from $83.98 on Nov. 20, per [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/27/brent-oil-wti-hormuz-middle-east.html) and Yahoo Finance data. Brent settled at $95.44 and gained 3% for the week, CNBC reported, after attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and on Saudi energy sites.

**Cash: flat at ICI, outflows at Lipper**

U.S. money market fund assets rose $2.49 billion to $7.979 trillion in the six days to Tuesday, Nov. 24, the [Investment Company Institute](https://www.ici.org/research/stats/mmf) reported, and [Crane Data](https://k8.cranedata.com/resources/link-of-the-day/) described the total as flat. Government funds added $5.01 billion and prime funds lost $2.25 billion. That is still just below the record $8.016 trillion set in early November.

LSEG Lipper's broader fund count showed money market funds losing a net $49.42 billion in the week to Nov. 25, their third straight weekly outflow, Reuters reported. The two reports cover different sets of funds and different days, so they do not line up one to one.

**What left crypto**

- Spot bitcoin ETFs: $1.25 billion out from Monday to Wednesday, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data show, matching SoSoValue's count as compiled by [Pre-Tick](https://pre-tick.live/blog/bitcoin-etf-flows-this-week). That made seven straight days of outflows since Nov. 17, totaling $3.05 billion. BlackRock's IBIT accounted for about $1.01 billion of this week's total.
- Spot ether ETFs: $217.5 million out over the same three days, per [Farside](https://farside.co.uk/eth/), an eighth straight day of outflows on Wednesday, [Bloomingbit](https://en.bloomingbit.io/feed/news/125288) reported.
- Friday's ETF flows had not been posted by publication time.
- Stablecoins: USD-pegged supply, measured at 7 p.m. ET on [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/stablecoins), slipped from $282.50 billion on Nov. 20 to $281.93 billion on Thursday, down $0.58 billion. Tether's USDT shrank about $1.3 billion over seven days, while Circle's USDC grew about $0.4 billion. [Stablecoin Beat](https://stablecoinbeat.com/charts/market-cap/) put the total at $282.8 billion on Friday.

The stablecoin drop this week was small next to the [$17.2 billion decline](https://blackmint.markets/news/stablecoin-supply-drops-17-billion) in the month to Nov. 24.

**What to watch**

The November jobs report comes Friday, Dec. 4, ahead of the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting, TreasuryBonds.com noted. Friday's ETF flows are still to come from Farside, and ICI normally publishes its weekly money fund report on Wednesdays.

*In our opinion: prices and flows told different stories this week. Stocks and crypto rose, but the flow reports that are complete so far show stock funds, bitcoin ETFs and stablecoins losing money, with government bond funds one of the few groups taking money in. Friday's flow data will show whether any of the rally's buyers came in through these funds, and next week's jobs report tests the December hike bets that have kept the dollar firm.*

articles.title: UAE Sells First Digital Treasury Bonds, Raising $49 Million
articles.excerpt: The UAE's two-year dirham bonds yield 4.98%, were issued and settled on Euroclear's digital platform and will trade on Nasdaq Dubai.
articles.body_md:
The United Arab Emirates sold its first digital federal treasury bonds on Friday, raising 180 million dirhams, about $49 million, through Euroclear's digital platform, the [UAE Ministry of Finance said](https://mof.gov.ae/en/news/ministry-of-finance-issues-first-aed-denominated-digital-sovereign-treasury-bonds/).

The two-year bonds carry a 4.98% yield to maturity and will be listed on Nasdaq Dubai. For crypto readers, this is tokenization, recording a real-world asset on a ledger, done by a national government with its own debt.

## What Makes a Bond "Digital"

A digital bond is ordinary government debt whose record of ownership is kept on a distributed ledger, a shared database updated by several parties at once. The goal is faster issuance and settlement, the step where cash and the bond change hands.

Here, Euroclear's Digital Financial Market Infrastructure handled issuance and settlement. The ministry said the setup stays linked to traditional settlement and distribution systems, so the bonds can still trade on a regular exchange.

## Banks Behind the Deal

The six primary dealers, the banks that buy government debt at auction, each received an equal share: First Abu Dhabi Bank, Emirates NBD, Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank, Mashreq Bank, HSBC and Standard Chartered. The yield was set by reference to the ministry's regular bond auction.

Standard Chartered acted as settlement agent, Citi as issuing and paying agent and Emirates NBD as structuring agent, the ministry said. [The National](https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/markets/2026/11/27/uae-issues-first-dirham-denominated-digital-sovereign-treasury-bonds/) also reported the deal.

Mohamed bin Hadi Al Hussaini, minister of state for financial affairs, called it "a practical step towards exploring broader opportunities for using distributed ledger technologies in sovereign debt markets."

The digital sale was small next to the ministry's regular November auction, which sold 920 million dirhams of conventional bonds and sukuk, Islamic bonds, against bids of 3.04 billion dirhams.

Bitcoin stood near $60,220 at 11:49 a.m. ET, down 0.4% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: The bigger story is who did the work. Euroclear, Citi, Standard Chartered and six primary dealers ran a government bond on a ledger, with the yield tied to the regular auction. The ministry said it will study the results before future issues, so the next thing to watch is whether a second, larger digital sale follows.*

articles.title: XRP Ledger Lending Feature Wins Validator Majority, Eyes Dec. 11
articles.excerpt: LendingProtocol now needs two weeks above 80% validator support. It would let brokers make uncollateralized, fixed-term loans from single-asset vaults.
articles.body_md:
Native lending on the XRP Ledger moved a step closer on Friday. Validators gave the LendingProtocol amendment, and a companion update, majority support at 9:22 a.m. ET, starting a two-week clock that ends Dec. 11, according to data from a public XRP Ledger server queried by Black Mint.

If support holds, the ledger would gain built-in, fixed-term loans funded from pooled deposits. Lenders could then put stablecoins to work inside the ledger itself. The network holds more than $800 million of them, per [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/stablecoins/XRPL) at 11:55 a.m. ET.

## How an XRPL Amendment Passes

Changes to how the XRP Ledger processes transactions ship as amendments. Under the [ledger's rules](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/networks-and-servers/amendments), one passes only after it keeps support from more than 80% of trusted validators for two straight weeks. If support drops to 80% or below, the clock restarts.

The ledger checks votes at a "flag ledger," every 256th ledger, roughly every 15 minutes. The server showed both lending amendments with majority status from that checkpoint, but not yet enabled.

## What the Lending Feature Does

According to the [XRPL documentation](https://xrpl.org/resources/known-amendments#lendingprotocol), the protocol (spec XLS-66) offers fixed-term loans with no on-chain collateral. A loan broker checks borrowers' credit off the ledger, then lends from a vault, a pool that holds one asset.

That means the lender's protection depends on the broker's underwriting, not on automatic liquidation. The [XLS-66 specification](https://github.com/XRPLF/XRPL-Standards/tree/master/XLS-0066-lending-protocol) lets a broker post optional first-loss capital, its own money that absorbs part of a default before depositors do.

The V1_1 update makes new brokers use closed-ended vaults, with set phases for deposits, lending and withdrawals. It also counts interest only when borrowers actually pay it.

The vaults themselves come from a separate amendment, SingleAssetVault. It reached majority at 2:38 p.m. ET on Nov. 25, which points to Dec. 9 if support holds.

Ripple's RLUSD makes up about $742 million of that, per DefiLlama.

*In our opinion: The question worth chasing is who ends up holding the credit risk. With no collateral to sell, vault depositors lean on a broker's off-chain checks and whatever first-loss cover it posts. The first test is Dec. 9 for vaults and Dec. 11 for lending, and only if support stays above 80% until then.*

articles.title: Tether Buys $10 Million of Bitdeer Shares, Lifting Stake to 17.9%
articles.excerpt: An SEC filing shows Tether bought 3.7 million Bitdeer shares at about $2.69 on Nov. 25. The miner's stock closed at $17.83 in mid-June.
articles.body_md:
Tether bought 3,715,943 shares of bitcoin miner Bitdeer Technologies Group on Nov. 25 for about $10 million, lifting its stake to 41,445,453 Class A shares, or 17.9%, according to a [Schedule 13D/A filed Friday](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1899123/000110465926132244/0001104659-26-132244.txt) with the SEC.

The purchase puts the issuer of USDT, the largest stablecoin with about $173.6 billion in circulation per [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/stablecoins), deeper into a Nasdaq-listed mining stock whose shares closed at $3.05 that day, down from $17.83 on June 12, per [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BTDR/history/) data.

## Two Trades on One Day

The filing lists two open-market purchases by a Tether unit: 12,240 shares at $2.65 and 3,703,703 shares at $2.693. Together they cost about $10.01 million.

Tether's share count rose about 9.8% from the 37,729,510 shares it reported in June. Its percentage fell, though, from 19.7% to 17.9%, because Bitdeer had 231,794,894 Class A shares outstanding on Sept. 30, up from about 191 million used in the earlier filing, [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/tether-buys-bitdeer-shares-stake-17-9/) and [crypto.news](https://crypto.news/tether-bitdeer-10-million-stock-purchase/) noted.

## What a 13D Filing Tells Investors

SEC rules require anyone who gains beneficial ownership of more than 5% of a company's voting shares to file a Schedule 13D, according to the [SEC's Investor.gov](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/glossary/schedules-13d-and-13g). Some passive holders can file a shorter 13G instead. Any material change requires a prompt amendment, called a 13D/A. This one is Amendment No. 14 to a filing first made on June 6, 2024.

The reporting parties are Tether Global Investments Fund, its subsidiary Tether International and Giancarlo Devasini. They share voting and selling power over the shares. At the Nov. 25 close, the full stake was worth about $126 million, by Black Mint's calculation from the filing and Yahoo Finance prices.

Bitdeer shares were at about $3.12 at 11:49 a.m. ET Friday, per Yahoo Finance, in a session that ends early at 1 p.m. ET after Thanksgiving.

*In our opinion: The number that matters is $2.69, the price Tether paid for shares that closed at $17.83 in mid-June. A stablecoin issuer adding to a mining stock near its six-month low ties more of its own balance sheet to bitcoin mining, and at Wednesday's close the whole stake was worth about $126 million. The next marker is Bitdeer's share count: if it keeps growing, Tether's 17.9% shrinks again unless it buys more.*

articles.title: Brazil's B3 and Six Banks Plan Open BRL Stablecoin for Early 2027
articles.excerpt: Bradesco, BTG Pactual, Itaú, Safra, Santander and XP join B3 on a real-pegged token. Banco B3 will issue it, and other banks can join at launch.
articles.body_md:
Brazil's stock exchange operator B3 and six Brazilian banks and brokerages said Friday they will build Open BRL, a stablecoin tied to the Brazilian real, with operations targeted for the first quarter of 2027.

The partners are Bradesco, BTG Pactual, Itaú Unibanco, Safra, Santander and XP, according to [B3's announcement](https://www.b3.com.br/pt_br/noticias/bolsa-e-seis-instituicoes-financeiras-se-unem-para-criar-stablecoin-em-reais.htm). For crypto users, it means a real-denominated token backed by the country's main exchange group and a group of private lenders, instead of a single private issuer.

## How a Shared Bank Stablecoin Works

A stablecoin is a blockchain token built to hold a steady value against a currency, here the real. A user hands over reais to the issuer and receives tokens. Those tokens can move between wallets in minutes and can be traded back for reais.

In the first phase, B3 will run the technology and Banco B3, the bank inside the exchange group, will issue the token. The six partners will build connections to their own systems and test uses such as moving money and settling trades in digital assets. B3 said the project will include audit and backing mechanisms and anti-money-laundering controls.

The shared design is the point. B3 said a common standard should let banks using different technology platforms send value to one another. Luiz Masagão, B3's vice president of products and clients, said building a common infrastructure together "allows this agenda to advance in a coordinated way," in Black Mint's translation of the release.

## Open to Other Banks at Launch

Other financial firms will be able to join once the platform is running, Masagão said in an interview with Valor Econômico, as reported by [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/brazils-b3-enlists-itau-santander-and-four-other-firms-for-open-brl-stablecoin/). The founders will fund the project, but the amount has not been disclosed.

The plan replaces a narrower one. In July, CNN Brasil reported that B3 was preparing its own real-pegged token, B3RL, according to Unchained. Friday's release does not mention B3RL.

Bitcoin traded near $60,220 at 11:49 a.m. ET, down 0.4% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: Seven rival institutions agreeing on one token is the headline; getting them to agree on the rulebook is the real assignment. The governance rules, the size of each firm's investment and the reserve reporting are still unpublished, and those decide who carries the risk if something breaks. The date on our calendar is the first quarter of 2027, when Open BRL is due to go live.*

articles.title: France and Spain Inflation Slows More Than Forecast in November
articles.excerpt: France's harmonised rate fell to 3.2% and Spain's to 4.1%, both below Reuters poll forecasts, as fuel prices eased. The ECB meets Dec. 16-17.
articles.body_md:
Inflation in France and Spain slowed more than economists expected in November, flash estimates from the two countries' statistics agencies showed Friday. France's EU-harmonised rate fell to 3.2% from 3.7% in October, [INSEE said](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/9161375). Spain's fell to 4.1% from 4.9%, [INE said](https://www.ine.es/dyngs/Prensa/en/adIPC1126.htm).

Analysts polled by Reuters had expected 3.6% for France, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/french-preliminary-inflation-at-32-in-november-5053065). For Spain's national index, which also came in at 4.1%, the Reuters poll had expected 4.6%, according to a [separate Reuters report](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/spains-12month-euharmonised-inflation-falls-to-41-in-november-5053073).

## Fuel Prices Drove Both Slowdowns

In France, energy inflation eased to 19.2% from 24.1% as oil product prices slowed sharply, though gas prices rose faster, INSEE said. Services inflation dipped to 2.3% from 2.6%. Prices fell 0.7% from October.

In Spain, INE said the drop came mainly from lower prices for vehicle fuel and lubricants. Core inflation, which leaves out energy and unprocessed food, fell to 2.6% from 3.1%.

## What a Flash Estimate Is

A flash estimate is an early reading built from a partial sample of prices, released before the full data. INSEE publishes final November figures on Dec. 11. The harmonised index (HICP) uses the same method across EU countries so rates can be compared, and the European Central Bank [measures inflation](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/mopo/strategy/html/index.en.html) for its 2% target with the euro-area HICP.

The ECB's Governing Council holds its next policy meeting on [Dec. 16-17](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/calendars/mgcgc/html/index.en.html). Interest-rate decisions affect the cost of borrowing across markets, including for traders who use leverage on crypto and other risk assets.

Bitcoin traded at $61,561 at 5:48 a.m. ET, up 1.8% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: Two big euro economies both came in well under forecast, and both pointed to fuel, which gives the ECB softer numbers to weigh less than three weeks before it meets. The stake is the price of euro borrowing for households, companies and leveraged traders alike. The number that matters next is the euro-area flash estimate from Eurostat, and then the Dec. 17 decision.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Options Worth $6.8 Billion Settle Below Max Pain
articles.excerpt: Deribit's monthly bitcoin options settled at $61,600 at 3 a.m. ET, about $8,400 below the $70,000 level where buyers would collect the least.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin options worth about $6.8 billion on Deribit settled at 3 a.m. ET Friday at a bitcoin index price of [$61,600.17](https://www.deribit.com/api/v2/public/get_delivery_prices?index_name=btc_usd&count=3), according to the exchange's public data. That was $8,400 below the $70,000 "max pain" level that analytics firms [CryptoQuant](https://cryptoquant.com/insights/quicktake/6b08e5a853e00349d2214313-68-Billion-in-Bitcoin-Options-Expire-Friday-With-Max-Pain-at-70000) and [Castle Labs](https://castlelabs.io/research/bitcoin-options) calculated from open positions before the expiry.

## How a Monthly Expiry Works

A bitcoin option is a contract that gives its buyer the right to buy (a call) or sell (a put) bitcoin at a set price, called the strike, until a set date. Deribit's bitcoin options are cash-settled, paid in bitcoin, against its index price at 08:00 UTC on expiry day. Contracts whose strike is on the wrong side of that price expire worthless.

"Max pain" is the strike at which the open calls and puts together would pay their holders the least. Both firms describe it as a gauge of where positions sit, not a forecast.

## The Positions Going Into Friday

Castle Labs counted 112,794 BTC of open interest in the Nov. 27 contract, worth $6.83 billion at the index, out of about 443,700 BTC open across all Deribit bitcoin expiries. CryptoQuant put the expiry at 25.4% of all bitcoin options open interest. CryptoQuant and Castle Labs each put the put-to-call ratio at 0.83, meaning there were 83 bitcoin of puts open for every 100 of calls.

CryptoQuant tied the gap to the speed of the drop. It noted that bitcoin traded above $75,000 for most of October, and that much of the open interest still sat at strikes from that range. By CryptoQuant's count, the expiry's largest single strike, $65,000, held 5,428 BTC, mostly puts, which finished in the money (worth exercising) with the index below that level.

## Price After Settlement

Bitcoin traded at $61,561 at 5:48 a.m. ET, up 1.8% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). Deribit's daily settlement price was $60,512.14 a day earlier and $58,754.83 on Wednesday.

*In our opinion: For a level called "max pain," $70,000 stayed comfortably out of reach, and the index settled $8,400 below it. The stake was real money for holders of puts struck above $61,600, which finished in the money, and for the sellers on the other side who paid them. The number to watch next is the Dec. 25 quarterly expiry, which Castle Labs lists as the largest single expiry on Deribit's board.*

articles.title: Tokyo Core Inflation Hits 2.9%, Fastest Pace Since July 2025
articles.excerpt: Tokyo core prices rose 2.9% in November from 2.6% in October as energy costs jumped 9.5%. The Bank of Japan meets Dec. 17-18.
articles.body_md:
Consumer prices in Tokyo excluding fresh food rose 2.9% in November from a year earlier, up from 2.6% in October, [Japan's statistics bureau](https://www.e-stat.go.jp/stat-search/file-download?fileKind=2&statInfId=000040525998) said on Friday local time. It was the fastest rise since July 2025, though slightly below the 3.0% median forecast in a Reuters poll, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/core-inflation-in-japans-capital-accelerates-in-november-5052767).

## Power and Gas Bills Did the Lifting

Energy prices in the capital rose 9.5% from a year earlier, compared with 2.2% in October, according to the bureau's release. Electricity was up 9.5% and city gas 13.7%. Reuters said the jump came partly because government subsidies for power and gas bills ended.

Strip energy out as well, and the picture cools. The index excluding fresh food and energy, which the Bank of Japan watches as a gauge of underlying inflation, rose 2.5%, down from 2.6% in October. The all-items figure rose 2.8%.

## Why Tokyo Numbers Get Watched

Tokyo's figures arrive ahead of the national data, and Reuters said they are widely regarded as a leading indicator (an early signal) for prices across Japan. Core inflation in the capital has now stayed above the BOJ's 2% target for three straight months, Reuters said.

The BOJ raised its policy rate to 1.25% in September and holds its next two-day meeting ending Dec. 18, according to Reuters. Why should crypto readers care? A higher Japanese rate makes it more expensive to borrow yen, the low-cost funding that some traders use to buy riskier assets abroad.

Bitcoin traded near $61,450 at 11:50 p.m. ET Thursday, up 0.8% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: The headline went up, but the measure the BOJ cares about most slipped to 2.5%, so this report gives both sides of the December debate something to point to. The stake is the price of yen borrowing, which reaches well past Japan. The next number to watch is the national November inflation release, and then the Dec. 18 rate decision.*

articles.title: Ethereum Developers Set Dec. 15 Hoodi Test for Glamsterdam Upgrade
articles.excerpt: Core developers kept the contested EIP-8037 storage-fee change as written and set the last public test for Dec. 15, seven weeks after the original date.
articles.body_md:
Ethereum's core developers on Thursday set Dec. 15 at 2:12 p.m. ET as the date the Glamsterdam upgrade goes live on the Hoodi test network, after teams agreed to keep a disputed storage-fee rule unchanged. The test had first been planned for late October, according to [EtherWorld's summary](https://etherworld.co/ethereum-protocol-update-acdc-192/) of the All Core Developers Consensus call No. 192, [listed on the project's GitHub](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2305).

## The Rule Nobody Reopened

The fight was over [EIP-8037](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/EIPS/eip-8037.md), which raises the gas cost of creating new "state," the permanent data every Ethereum node has to keep. Gas is the unit Ethereum uses to price computing work. Under the proposal (as written on GitHub), each new byte of state costs 1,530 gas and a new account counts as 120 bytes, which works out to 183,600 gas for that part alone.

The authors say the goal is to stop the database from growing too fast as blocks get bigger. The EIP says a Geth node's state was about 390 gigabytes in January and could pass 650 gigabytes, the level where nodes start to slow down, in under a year at a 200 million gas limit.

The catch is older smart contracts. Programs written around today's prices can run out of gas partway through a transaction. No alternative won enough support, so teams kept the specification as written, EtherWorld and [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/11/27/ethereum-s-much-awaited-glamsterdam-upgrade-cleared-for-december-test-here-s-what-to-know) reported.

## No Mainnet Date Yet

Developers have not set a date for the main network. The Sepolia test network already upgraded in October.

The same call reopened a debate over FOCIL, a feature planned for the following upgrade, Hegota, meant to stop block builders from leaving out valid transactions. Erigon, Geth, Prysm and other teams opposed keeping it in Hegota, EtherWorld reported, and Ethlabs researcher Caspar Schwarz-Schilling argued the engineering time is needed for quantum-resistant cryptography. A decision is expected on the next consensus call around Dec. 10, EtherWorld said.

Ether traded near $1,734 at 11:50 p.m. ET Thursday, up 1.9% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum).

*In our opinion: Seven weeks late, Glamsterdam now has a dress rehearsal on the calendar, and the cast was told the script will not change. The people carrying the risk are teams running older contracts that assume cheap storage, since they have until Dec. 15 to check their code. Watch the Hoodi fork at 2:12 p.m. ET that day, then whether developers pick a mainnet date.*

articles.title: ASEAN+3 Sets Up Working Group on Digital Payments and Crypto Rules
articles.excerpt: Finance and central bank deputies from 14 Asian economies agreed in Kyoto to launch a program on cross-border payments and digital asset rules.
articles.body_md:
Finance and central bank deputies from the 11 ASEAN members plus China, Japan and South Korea agreed in Kyoto this week to set up a working group on cross-border digital payments and how to regulate digital assets, according to a [co-chairs' statement](https://www.mof.go.jp/english/policy/international_policy/convention/others/CochairsStatement.pdf) released Thursday by Japan's Ministry of Finance.

The group sits under a new AMRO Cross-Border Digital Payments Program. AMRO, the ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office, is the Singapore-based body that monitors the region's economies and supports its emergency currency-swap arrangement.

## What the Group Will Actually Study

The statement says the program will advance policy talks on two kinds of payment links. Retail links cover everyday transfers, such as a tourist paying a shop or a worker sending money home. Wholesale links cover large payments between banks and financial institutions.

AMRO has already started on the first piece. A [consultancy notice](https://www.amro-asia.org/consultant-on-cross-border-retail-payments) it posted on Nov. 18 describes a gap analysis that will map existing payment links in the region and look for what blocks wider connections. Listed use cases: person-to-person payments, payments to merchants, tourism spending, cross-border online shopping and remittances.

## From Uzbekistan to Kyoto

Ministers and central bank governors meeting in Uzbekistan in May told their deputies to set up a way to discuss payment connectivity and regulatory approaches to stablecoins by the end of 2026, [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-11-26-china-japan-south-korea-asean-digital-payments-447029) and [crypto.news](https://crypto.news/asean-china-japan-south-korea-digital-payments/) reported. The Kyoto meeting was the last one scheduled under this year's co-chairs, Japan and the Philippines.

The working group does not write rules. Its results go to finance ministers and central bank governors at their next meeting in Nagoya, Japan, in May 2027, according to the statement.

*In our opinion: Payment links in the region are a patchwork of bilateral and multilateral deals, and now all 14 economies have a standing forum that covers digital assets too. Payment firms and stablecoin issuers have the most riding on it, because a shared approach would shape whether they face one set of expectations across the region or 14 different ones. The date to watch is the Nagoya ministers' meeting in May 2027, where any shared position would first surface.*

articles.title: Euro Leaders Back Spain's Hernández de Cos to Succeed Lagarde at ECB
articles.excerpt: Euro area governments picked the Bank for International Settlements chief on Thursday. Formal appointment is due in December, ahead of Lagarde's Feb. 7 exit.
articles.body_md:
Euro area leaders on Thursday agreed to recommend Pablo Hernández de Cos, a former Bank of Spain governor, as the next president of the European Central Bank. He would replace Christine Lagarde, who steps down on Feb. 7, 2027.

European Council President António Costa announced the pick on X and said it opens the door to formally appointing the new ECB leadership in December, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/euro-countries-pick-spains-de-cos-as-ecb-chief-costa-says-5052656). The same package recommends France's Laurence Boone and Germany's Markus Brunnermeier for the ECB's six-member Executive Board, according to Reuters and [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/eu-reaches-consensus-on-spains-hernandez-de-cos-as-next-ecb-chief-report/4139550).

## Netherlands Drops Knot Bid

The Netherlands had pushed its own former central bank governor, Klaas Knot, before backing the deal at this week's summit in Brussels, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/26/pablo-hernandez-de-cos-ecb-president.html) and Anadolu reported. Hernández de Cos now runs the Bank for International Settlements, the Basel-based bank that serves the world's central banks.

## How an ECB President Gets the Job

Nobody votes for the post directly. Euro area governments recommend a candidate, then consult the European Parliament and the ECB's Governing Council before EU leaders make the formal appointment, according to CNBC and Anadolu.

The job reaches well past Europe. The ECB sets interest rates for the countries that use the euro and aims to keep inflation at 2% over the medium term. Its rate decisions move euro borrowing costs and the euro's exchange rate against the dollar.

Bitcoin traded near $60,590 at 5:50 p.m. ET, up 0.8% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: The name is settled, but the paperwork is not. The bigger story is that France, Germany and Spain filled three of the ECB's top seats in one deal, so the bank's chief, chief economist and markets head all change in 2027. For crypto readers, the date to circle is Feb. 7, when the person whose rate calls help set the euro's value against the dollar changes for the first time in more than seven years.*

articles.title: Binance Lifts Withdrawal Halt Four Weeks After $6.3 Billion Hack
articles.excerpt: The exchange said recovery work is complete. Researchers cited by Reuters put stolen funds routed through THORChain above $600 million.
articles.body_md:
Binance said Thursday it has fully lifted the withdrawal suspension it put in place after hackers took an estimated $6.3 billion from the exchange on Oct. 29, 28 days earlier.

"Our withdrawal recovery work is completed," the exchange said in a [service update](https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/detail/95c463396a034f1ab3994814225e6d69). It said withdrawals on a small number of networks remain paused for maintenance or planned upgrades, separate from the recovery, affecting "a very small percentage of regular traffic." [Reuters](https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/companies-markets/banking-finance/binance-lifts-withdrawal-suspension-after-us6-3-billion-crypto-heist) also reported the reopening. Binance said in the update that user assets "remain fully backed and accounted for."

## Why Exchanges Freeze Withdrawals

Exchanges keep part of customer funds in hot wallets, which stay connected to the internet so withdrawals can go out quickly. The October attack drained Binance hot wallets on more than 10 blockchains in about 20 minutes, according to researchers cited by [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/thorchain-north-korea-binance-hack-laundering/). A withdrawal freeze stops more money from leaving while a platform rebuilds and checks its systems.

The FBI attributed the theft on Oct. 31 to TraderTraitor, a hacking group linked to North Korea, Crypto Briefing reported. Reuters also described the attackers as North Korean hackers.

## Stolen Funds Move Through THORChain

More than $600 million of the stolen funds has passed through THORChain, Reuters reported, citing blockchain researchers, according to [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-hack-flows-through-thorchain-top-600m-reuters) and Crypto Briefing. THORChain is a decentralized exchange that swaps tokens between blockchains without a company holding the money in between. The Defiant noted the estimate may count some funds more than once, and that the FBI had asked THORChain node operators to block transactions tied to the theft.

A response from THORChain to the figures was not included in the reports Black Mint reviewed.

BNB, the token tied to Binance's ecosystem, traded near $555 at 5:50 p.m. ET, up 0.4% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bnb).

*In our opinion: Reopened withdrawals answer the first question for Binance customers, though the update itself says a few networks are still paused. The trail of the stolen money is still being mapped, and the $600 million THORChain estimate comes with a double-counting caveat. Binance points users to its network status page before moving funds, which is worth checking first.*

articles.title: Zodia Custody Says Unauthorized Party Accessed Client Contacts
articles.excerpt: Standard Chartered's crypto custodian said it took its client API offline after detecting probing on Nov. 23 and has found no unauthorized transactions.
articles.body_md:
Zodia Custody, the crypto custodian owned by Standard Chartered, said Thursday that an unauthorized party accessed contact details for a small number of clients and employees on Nov. 24. It said no unauthorized transactions have been found so far.

Zodia has not reported any loss of client assets. Names and work email addresses can be used for phishing, where criminals pose as a trusted firm to trick staff into handing over logins or approving transfers.

**Probing began on Nov. 23**

Zodia detected attempts to probe its platform on Nov. 23, CEO Richard Clark said in a [company statement](https://zodia-custody.com/statement-on-recent-security-incident/). As a precaution, the firm took its B2B API offline, added security measures and then restored the service. Monitoring the next day found that an unauthorized party had accessed "limited client information."

That information consisted of publicly available organization details and, for a small number of clients and employees, a business contact name and email address, Clark said. "Based on our investigation to date, there have been no unauthorised transactions," he said. Zodia has contacted its clients and informed regulators, according to the statement and [Finextra's summary of Reuters reporting](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48820/client-data-leaked-in-zodia-custody-security-breach---reuters).

**What a custody API does**

A custodian holds digital assets for funds, banks and companies and keeps the private keys that control them. An API, short for application programming interface, is the link that lets a client's own software connect directly to the custodian's platform. Taking it offline cuts that automated connection while engineers check for weak points.

Zodia did not say who was behind the incident or how the information was accessed, [Decrypt reported](https://decrypt.co/384033/standard-chartereds-zodia-custody-says-hackers-accessed-client-contact-details). Standard Chartered recently raised its stake in Zodia to 100%, according to [Finextra](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48820/client-data-leaked-in-zodia-custody-security-breach---reuters) and [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/11/26/standard-chartered-s-zodia-custody-suffers-data-breach-exposing-client-information).

*In our opinion: The figure that carries this story is zero, the count of unauthorized transactions Zodia has found to date. The practical risk now sits with client staff, who could receive messages that look like they come from Zodia, so confirming any unexpected request through a known channel is sensible. The next thing to watch is whether Zodia or its regulators publish how the access happened.*
